assessment: This is an important article with compelling experimental methods, including ethologically relevant behavior, sophisticated physiological methods including optogenetic suppression of primary visual cortical activity, careful behavioral experiments, and clear, convincing, quantitative analysis of the resulting data. The article enhances our understanding of the role of active visual estimation of distance under multiple factors of visual degradation (binocular/monocular, and V1 suppression), demonstrating how robust task performance can emerge from compensatory active sensing strategies.
